args.text: I am from Ukraine and I speak Ukrainian and Russian. Now I live in Brno and work as a logistics coordinator. I have worked there since three years. I am responsible about deliveries and I contact carriers when a truck is late. Then I tell my team the new delivery time so we can change our plan.

args.text: Then our team informs the customer about new delivery time. We change the plan in our system and check if warehouse can receive the goods later. If there is a big delay, we look for another solution together.

args.text: First I ask the warehouse when they can receive the goods. Then I call the carrier and try to agree a new time. If driver cannot wait, I check with my team if we can use another warehouse. I keep the customer informed about the delay.

args.text: Usually yes, if warehouse can receive the truck later. If it is too late, we arrange delivery for next morning. I explain the reason to customer and confirm the new time with carrier.

args.text: In the morning I call the carrier and ask where the driver is. Then I check with warehouse if the goods arrived. If there is another delay, I inform customer and my team immediately.

criteria.evidence: facts.placement is null. The journey ends with a rehearsal recap, not a band: #11 "8 replies; 0 moments to keep."

#2 "I am from Ukraine and I speak Ukrainian and Russian" receives a work-focused response at #3: "What does your team do next?" No shown tutor line assumes Czech nationality or childhood. Mixed-language handling was not tested.
Although interview is sixth in #1, her selection is honoured at #2: "Your partner: Jordan · Interviewer."
Accessible, realistic logistics questions include #4 "What do you do if the warehouse says no?" and #6 "How do you check that the goods arrive the next morning?" Interview depth is limited.
#2 includes "since three years" and "responsible about deliveries," but no correction follows. #11 confirms "0 moments to keep."
#2 explicitly allows "a made-up example." Subsequent questions concern work, such as #7 "Who helps you if you cannot reach the driver?" No sensitive displacement or status details are requested.

boundaries.notes: No defined breach appears. Pitch has zero counted units because facts.conversation is absent. Moment recall uses the eight learner replies in steps #2–#9; each contains a clear error and receives neither a moment nor coaching.

findings.title: The promised level check ends as an unassessed rehearsal
findings.expected: Reach a credible placement band, personal summary and next focus from the first visit.
findings.got: Choosing an interview opens a conversation; finishing produces only a rehearsal count. No placement is saved.
findings.evidence: #1 "Let's find your level: three questions about you, then a few short tasks"; #11 "Rehearsal saved: Your part in a team. 8 replies; 0 moments to keep." Her final reaction is "I still don't see my level."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Following the first-visit level-check invitation through any offered situation reaches an assessed band and evidence-based next focus.

findings.title: Clear interview-language errors receive no coaching
findings.expected: Selective, correct feedback on recurring errors that affect her interview answers.
findings.got: All eight learner replies contain clear errors, but the tutor only continues questioning and saves no moments.
findings.evidence: #2 "I have worked there since three years" and "I am responsible about deliveries"; #8 "what is the problem" inside an indirect question; #11 "0 moments to keep."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Provide selective coaching such as "for three years" and "responsible for deliveries," with a chance to reuse the corrected interview language.

findings.title: Follow-up questions keep extending one scenario
findings.expected: Use her substantial answers to assess her English and bring the check to a clear conclusion.
findings.got: The tutor follows increasingly small procedural details without giving an assessment or a visible endpoint.
findings.evidence: #9 "How do you thank her after she helps?"; #10 "When she has too much work, what do you do first?" She finishes with "We keep repeating the same situation, and I want to know how ready I am for Friday."
findings.suggested_acceptance: After sufficient connected language, conclude the assessment and explain the band using examples from her answers.

findings.title: Her identity is respected and her work supplies the context
findings.expected: Treat her as an adult professional without assumptions about nationality or displacement.
findings.got: The tutor accepts her introduction and builds understandable questions around carriers, warehouses and delivery coordination.
findings.evidence: #2 "You can use a made-up example"; #4 "What do you do if the warehouse says no?"; #7 "Who helps you if you cannot reach the driver?"
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve optional fictional examples and work-focused adaptation without asking about immigration or displacement.

judge.voice: I would use it again only if it actually finishes the level check. The warehouse and carrier questions were familiar, and I could explain my work without being treated as a Czech learner or a refugee case. That mattered. But after eight answers, I still had no level, no explanation of my readiness and no corrections to practise before Friday. We kept following the same delivery problem until we were discussing how I thank a colleague. I need useful feedback, not just another question. I cannot trust a level I never received or judge corrections that never appeared. I got some rehearsal, but I could also speak those answers in front of a mirror. This session did not show enough coaching value to justify more time. I would not yet recommend it for interview preparation.

judge.voice: I need English for Friday, and I spent this session changing classes and meal plans. I explained my job clearly, but my first request was called invalid. Shorter requests finally gave me two useful situations: explaining my logistics experience and calling a carrier about a late truck. Those sounded like my work. Then the swaps kept returning things I had already rejected, and I left without agreeing a plan. Questions about the team, salary and shifts were still missing. Nobody made assumptions about my nationality, which I appreciated. I cannot judge the level or corrections because I never reached practice. There is no useful rehearsal here to justify the effort; the transcript does not establish waiting time. I would try the two work topics directly, but I would not recommend this planning flow to a colleague preparing for an interview.

judge.voice: I could follow Maya easily, and she remembered my order and that I was in a hurry. The English felt suitable for me, and nobody treated me as a child or assumed I was Czech. But I need an interview rehearsal for Friday. I finished eight replies about chicken and still had that work waiting. I also wrote “How long it will take?” and got no correction. A saved reply count does not tell me what to improve. I trust the difficulty more than the teaching after this session. I would try the interview option once, but I would not yet recommend this for preparing for a logistics role. There is no evidence here to judge the waits, and I cannot claim it saved interview-preparation time.
